draft.title: Community legal centres
card: Community legal centres (CLCs) are independent, non-profit services. They give free legal help to people in their community.
CLCs help accused people and victims of crime. They can give advice, information and, in some cases, representation.
They are independent of Victoria Legal Aid. Many help people who cannot get a lawyer through Legal Aid.
Some CLCs serve a local area. Others focus on a group, such as young people or people on low incomes.
draft.remember: CLCs are free, independent services that often help where Legal Aid does not.

a.q: Which description best fits a community legal centre?
opts: An independent service giving free legal help
A court that hears minor criminal cases
A government body that prosecutes accused people
A private firm that charges standard fees
a.why: CLCs are independent services that give free legal help to accused people and victims. A private firm charging fees is wrong because CLCs do not charge for this help. They also do not prosecute or hear cases.
a.clue: Think about who runs them and what they charge.

b.q: Jess is accused of a driving offence. VLA will not fund a lawyer for her, and she cannot afford a private one. What could she do?
opts: Ask a local community legal centre for free help
Wait for the court to appoint her a free lawyer
Ask the prosecution to give her legal advice
Plead guilty because no help is available
b.why: CLCs often help people who cannot get Legal Aid, so Jess can ask one for free help. Pleading guilty is wrong because help may still be available. The prosecution acts against her, so it cannot advise her.
b.clue: Which service often helps people that Legal Aid cannot?

a.best: An independent service giving free legal help

b.best: Ask a local community legal centre for free help
